title: 2017 AMC 12B Problem 11
statement: Call a positive integer monotonous if it is a one-digit number or its digits, when read from left to right, form either a strictly increasing or a strictly decreasing sequence. For example, \(3,\) \(23578,\) and \(987620\) are monotonous, but \(88,\) \(7434,\) and \(23557\) are not. How many monotonous positive integers are there?

solutions.text:
Strictly increasing monotonous numbers correspond to nonempty subsets of \(\{1, \ldots, 9\},\) giving \(2^9 - 1 = 511.\) Strictly decreasing ones correspond to subsets of \(\{0, 1, \ldots, 9\}\) other than \(\varnothing\) and \(\{0\}\) (a leading \(0\) is not allowed), giving \(2^{10} - 2 = 1022.\) The nine single-digit numbers are counted in both, so the total is \(511 + 1022 - 9 = 1524.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Each nonempty subset of \(\{1, 2, \ldots, 9\}\) gives exactly one strictly increasing number
Decreasing numbers correspond to subsets of \(\{0, 1, \ldots, 9\}\) except \(\varnothing\) and \(\{0\};\) single digits are counted twice
